You are simplifying and refocusing the PUBLIC marketing site for Nxeon, a premium cloud VPS host (Next.js 15 + Tailwind v4) at /opt/nxeon. Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first. The user's feedback: the landing is TOO CLUTTERED — make it as simple and easy as possible, don't confuse people. Also: heavily advertise GAME SERVERS (their own prominent section) and a new "build anything with Claude AI, no code" capability. Use REAL logos. Keep the premium dark aesthetic (glass, navy #060a14, blue→purple gradients).

STRICT SCOPE — ONLY modify: app/page.tsx, app/(marketing)/** (features/pricing/about/contact/vps/domains), components/marketing/**. Do NOT touch app/dashboard, app/admin, app/api, lib/, worker/, prisma/, components/ui/ (EXCEPT you may IMPORT the new `AppLogo` from `@/components/ui/AppLogo`), components/portal/, globals.css, configs. Do NOT run build/git/systemctl. You MAY run `npx tsc --noEmit`.

KEY CHANGES:
1. **Declutter the landing (app/page.tsx).** It currently has many dense sections. Cut it to a clean, scannable flow that a non-technical visitor instantly gets: (a) a bold simple hero with ONE clear value prop + one primary CTA (Get started) + one secondary (View pricing); (b) 3–4 big benefit tiles (not 8); (c) a short "deploy anything" strip; (d) simple pricing (the 4 plans); (e) the game-servers section; (f) the Claude AI section; (g) CTA + footer. Remove redundancy, shorten copy, more whitespace, fewer competing elements. Prioritize clarity over showing everything.
2. **Game servers — prominent dedicated section.** Showcase one-click game hosting (Minecraft, Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2, Terraria) with a clean tile grid, "deploy in minutes, low latency" copy, and a CTA. Make it feel like a headline offering, not a footnote.
3. **Claude AI builder — new hero-level feature section.** Advertise: "Build anything on your server with a single prompt — no code." The idea: customers can connect Claude to their VPS and describe what they want built, and it happens. Write compelling, simple copy + a visual (e.g. a prompt box mock → result). Position it as a flagship differentiator. Add it to the top feature tiles too. (This is aspirational marketing for a feature being built — keep copy truthful/near-term: "connect Claude to your server and build with plain English.")
4. **Real logos:** replace any emoji/placeholder brand marks with `<AppLogo family="..." name="..." />` from `@/components/ui/AppLogo` (families: ubuntu, debian, almalinux, rocky, docker, wordpress, nextcloud, nodejs, caddy, wireguard, cpanel, plesk, minecraft, etc. — it renders real SVGs from /public/logos with a fallback).
5. **Fix false/placeholder copy** (deep-audit findings): remove "Dedicated IPv4 on every plan" (it's a paid add-on now — say "optional dedicated IPv4" instead) and "isolated private networking" (VMs share a NAT bridge). Remove any visible "Placeholder copy"/"this form has no backend" text and the contact-form dead end (make the contact page show a real support email + note tickets in-dashboard). Tone "global reach" down to "Singapore datacenter, more coming".

Read live plans/images from Prisma (read-only import of `@/lib/db`), `export const dynamic="force-dynamic"`. Fully responsive, simple, fast. tsc clean. Report files changed + confirm tsc passes.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Commands
36	
37	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
38	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
39	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
40	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
41	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
42	
43	## Domains & TLS
44	
45	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
46	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
47	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
48	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
49	
50	## Environments
51	
52	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
53	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
54	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
55	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
56	
57	## Safety rules
58	
59	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
60	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
61	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
62	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
63	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
64	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
